| 假 (jiǎ) | 造假 | zào jiǎ | To fabricate; to falsify; to manufacture fakes. | The verb 造 (to make, to manufacture) combined with 假 produces a common expression for the act of creating false documents, data, or objects. | 假 (jiǎ) | 掺假 | chān jiǎ | To adulterate; to mix in fake or inferior material. | The verb 掺 (to mix in, to adulterate) combined with 假 describes the practice of mixing counterfeit or inferior material into genuine goods. | 假 (jiǎ) | 作假 | zuò jiǎ | To falsify; to cheat; to engage in deception. | The verb 作 (to do, to engage in) combined with 假 produces a common expression for deliberate falsification or cheating. | 假 (jiǎ) | 说假话 | shuō jiǎhuà | To tell a lie; to speak falsely. | The standard verb-object collocation for lying or making false statements. Directly contrasts with 说真话. Extremely common across all registers. | [CORE] |
| 假 (jiǎ) | 辨别真假 | biànbié zhēnjiǎ | To distinguish the genuine from the fake; to tell real from false. | A common verb-object collocation used in authentication, commercial, and analytical contexts. | 假 (jiǎ) | 辨真假 | biàn zhēnjiǎ | To distinguish the genuine from the fake; to tell real from false. | A verb-object construction using 辨 (to distinguish) + 真假, meaning to evaluate and determine whether something is authentic or counterfeit. | 真实 (zhēnshí) | 还原真实 | huányuán zhēnshí | To restore the truth; to recover the authentic state of affairs; to reconstruct what actually happened. | The verb 还原 (to restore, to return to the original state) combined with 真实 describes the act of recovering an accurate account of events or an authentic representation. | 真实 (zhēnshí) | 贴近真实 | tiējìn zhēnshí | To be close to reality; to approximate the truth; to be true to life. | The verb phrase 贴近 (to be close to, to approach) combined with 真实 evaluates a representation or account as approximating reality. | 真实 (zhēnshí) | 反映真实情况 | fǎnyìng zhēnshí qíngkuàng | To reflect the true situation; to accurately represent the actual state of affairs. | The verb 反映 (to reflect, to represent) combined with 真实情况 (true situation) is a standard collocation in journalistic, administrative, and legal discourse for evaluating whether a report or account accurately captures reality. 真实 functions as an attributive modifier within the object noun phrase. | [CORE] |
| 真实 (zhēnshí) | 追求真实 | zhuīqiú zhēnshí | To pursue authenticity; to seek the truth. | The verb 追求 (to pursue, to seek) combined with 真实 expresses an orientation toward authentic representation or factual accuracy. Common in artistic, journalistic, and philosophical discourse. | [CORE] |
| 真实 (zhēnshí) | 基于真实事件 | jīyú zhēnshí shìjiàn | Based on true events; based on a true story. | A prepositional phrase construction extremely common in film, literature, and media to indicate that a narrative is grounded in actual events. | 真实 (zhēnshí) | 与真实不符 | yǔ zhēnshí bù fú | Inconsistent with reality; not in accordance with the facts. | A prepositional construction used in legal and evaluative contexts to characterize a statement or representation as deviating from factual reality. | 虚假 (xūjiǎ) | 虚假广告 | xūjiǎ guǎnggào | False advertising; fraudulent advertisement. | A standard collocation in Chinese consumer protection and advertising law. 虚假广告 is a legal term of art appearing in the Advertising Law (广告法) and related regulations. | 虚假 (xūjiǎ) | 虚假宣传 | xūjiǎ xuānchuán | False advertising; fraudulent publicity. | A fixed noun phrase used in consumer protection and regulatory law to describe advertising or promotional claims that are misleading or factually false. | 虚假 (xūjiǎ) | 散布虚假消息 | sànbù xūjiǎ xiāoxi | To spread false news; to disseminate misinformation. | A verb-object construction used in legal and journalistic contexts, particularly in discussions of rumor-spreading and online misinformation. Common in regulatory and media discourse. | [CORE] |
| 虚假 (xūjiǎ) | 发布虚假广告 | fābù xūjiǎ guǎnggào | To publish false advertising; to issue fraudulent advertisements. | A verb-object construction used in consumer protection and regulatory contexts. 虚假广告 (false/fraudulent advertising) is a standard legal category in Chinese advertising law. | [CORE] |
| 虚假 (xūjiǎ) | 散布虚假信息 | sànbù xūjiǎ xìnxī | To spread false information; to disseminate disinformation. | A verb-object construction with 散布 (to spread/disseminate) + 虚假信息 (false information), used in legal, regulatory, and journalistic contexts. | 正确 (zhèngquè) | 基本正确 | jīběn zhèngquè | Basically correct; largely accurate; correct in its essentials. | A degree-modified predicate construction using 基本 (basically, fundamentally) to qualify the assertion of correctness, indicating that something is correct in its main points though perhaps not in every detail. | 错误 (cuòwù) | 纠正错误 | jiūzhèng cuòwù | To correct an error; to rectify a mistake. | The verb 纠正 (to correct, to rectify) combined with 错误 is a standard collocation in educational, political, and everyday discourse. | 错误 (cuòwù) | 承认错误 | chéngrèn cuòwù | To admit a mistake; to acknowledge an error. | The verb 承认 (to admit, to acknowledge) combined with 错误 is a standard collocation in interpersonal, legal, and political discourse. | 错误 (cuòwù) | 严重错误 | yánzhòng cuòwù | A serious error; a grave mistake. | A fixed attributive construction using 严重 (serious, grave) to intensify the evaluation of an error. | 准确 (zhǔnquè) | 做到准确无误 | zuòdào zhǔnquè wúwù | To achieve accuracy without error; to be completely accurate. | The fixed collocation 准确无误 (accurate and without error) is a common intensified form used in technical, legal, and administrative contexts to assert complete precision. 做到 (to achieve, to manage to) introduces it as a goal or standard. | [CORE] |
| 准确 (zhǔnquè) | 无法准确判断 | wúfǎ zhǔnquè pànduàn | Unable to make an accurate judgment; cannot judge precisely. | 准确 functioning as an adverbial modifier before a verb of judgment or assessment is a highly productive pattern: 准确判断 (to judge accurately), 准确预测 (to predict accurately), 准确描述 (to describe accurately). The negated form with 无法 or 不能 is equally common. | [CORE] |
| 准确 (zhǔnquè) | 表述准确 | biǎoshù zhǔnquè | The formulation is accurate; the expression is precise. | A predicate construction used in academic, legal, and editorial contexts to evaluate whether a statement or formulation is precisely worded. 准确 functions as a predicate adjective. | 准确 (zhǔnquè) | 准确把握 | zhǔnquè bǎwò | To accurately grasp; to have a precise understanding of. | A common adverb-verb construction used in analytical contexts. | [CORE] |

|------|----------------|-----------------|--------------------|--------------------|-----------------|
| אֱמֶת | ʾemet | truth, faithfulness; root א-מ-ת (ʾ-m-t), related to firmness, reliability | truth, truthfulness, veracity, authenticity, faithfulness, reality, genuineness | The most central and widely used Hebrew term for truth, appearing across biblical, rabbinic, legal, religious, philosophical, and everyday modern contexts. It can describe a true statement, a genuine object, a reliable person, or a quality of genuine reliability. In rabbinic literature it is also treated as a foundational moral value. Appears in fixed expressions such as *ʾemet ve-ʾemuna* ("truth and faithfulness"), *ʾemet ve-shalom* ("truth and peace"), and *le-ʾamet* (to verify/confirm). Participates in extensive derivational patterns. | [CORE] |
| אמיתי | ʾamiti | true, real, genuine; adjectival form derived from *ʾemet* | true, real, genuine, authentic | The standard modern Hebrew adjective meaning "true" or "genuine," used attributively and predicatively across registers. It applies to statements, objects, feelings, and identities, and is used to describe persons, feelings, objects, or states as genuinely what they appear to be. Frequently used in everyday speech to distinguish the real from the fake or the sincere from the performative. Slightly more colloquial than *ʾemet* itself. Contrasts with *medumaʾ* ("imagined"), *meumat* ("fabricated"), and *mezuyaf* ("forged/fake"). Example: *ʾohev ʾamitʾi* ("a true/genuine friend"). | [CORE] |
| נכון | nakhon | correct, right, established; root כ-ו-נ (k-w-n), to be established, prepared, firm, correct | correct, right, accurate, true, proper | Widely used to evaluate statements, answers, facts, and procedures as accurate or correct, particularly in everyday and educational contexts. It is the standard response to confirm that something is accurate or has been done properly. Also carries a sense of moral or practical rightness in some collocations, e.g., *ze lo nakhon* ("that's not right/correct"). Less philosophically weighted than *ʾemet* but extremely frequent. Participates in derivations such as *nekhonah* (f.) and *le-nakhen* ("to correct"). | [CORE] |
| מדויק | meduyaq | precise, exact; Pu'al/Mefuʿal passive participle from root ד-י-ק (d-y-q), related to fineness, exactness | accurate, precise, exact | Used to evaluate the degree of correspondence between a representation, measurement, statement, description, or translation and the reality or standard it describes. Common in scientific, technical, journalistic, and legal contexts. Implies a higher standard of exactness than *nakhon*. Contrasts with *meʿurpal* ("vague") or *meshuʿar* ("approximate"). Example: *tiʾur meduyaq* ("an accurate description"). The root also yields *diyuq* ("precision, exactness") and *ledayeq* ("to be precise"). | [CORE] |
| אותנטי | ʾotenti | authentic; loanword from Greek/Latin *authenticus* via European languages | authentic, genuine | A borrowing used in modern Hebrew, especially in cultural, artistic, philosophical, and psychological contexts, to evaluate whether something is genuine or original rather than derivative or imitative. More restricted in register than *ʾamiti* and tends to appear in educated, academic, or journalistic discourse. Sometimes interchangeable with *meqori* in aesthetic contexts. Common in discussions of personal identity or cultural heritage. Functions as a direct parallel to English "authentic." | [CORE] |
| מקורי | meqori | original; derived from מָקוֹר (*maqor*, source, origin); root ק-ו-ר (q-w-r) | original, genuine, authentic | Describes something that is the original rather than a copy or imitation, and by extension something that is genuinely creative or not derivative. Used in aesthetic, legal (intellectual property), and commercial evaluation to evaluate whether something is an original rather than a copy. Can describe artworks, documents, ideas, or personal style. Overlaps with *ʾotenti* in some contexts but emphasizes origin rather than genuineness of character per se. Example: *yetsirah meqorit* ("an original work"). Contrasts with *ha-ʿataqah* ("the copy") or *ziyyuf* ("forgery"). | [CORE] |
| אמין | ʾamin | reliable, trustworthy; adjectival form from root א-מ-נ (ʾ-m-n), same root family as *ʾemet* | reliable, trustworthy, credible, dependable | Closely related to *mehiman* but somewhat more colloquial and broadly used. Applied to persons, sources, witnesses, systems, and information to indicate dependability and accuracy. Common in modern Hebrew in contexts such as journalism, law, and everyday evaluation of people. Contrasts with *lo ʾamin* (unreliable). The noun *ʾaminut* is the standard modern Hebrew term for "reliability" or "credibility." | [CORE] |
| אמינות | ʾaminut | reliability, trustworthiness; abstract noun from root א-מ-נ (ʾ-m-n) | reliability, credibility, trustworthiness | Refers to the quality of being believable and dependable, applied to persons, institutions, sources, and testimony. Central in legal and journalistic discourse when evaluating the weight to be given to a witness or source. A key term in legal evaluation of witnesses (*ʾaminut ha-ʿed*, "the credibility of the witness") and in journalistic and academic assessment of sources. Frequently appears in the phrase *behinat ha-ʾaminut* ("examination of credibility"). Closely related to *mehiman* and *neʾeman*. | [CORE] |
| מהימן | mehiman | trustworthy, reliable; Hif'il participial form from root א-מ-נ (ʾ-m-n), to trust, be faithful | reliable, trustworthy, credible | Evaluates persons, sources, witnesses, and information as trustworthy and credible. Used especially in legal and formal contexts to describe witnesses, testimony, or sources deemed credible. Slightly more formal than *ʾamin* and more common in written legal Hebrew. Common in legal testimony contexts (*ʿed mehiman*, "a credible witness") and in journalism. Shares a root with *ʾemet* and *ʾemunah*. The noun *mehimanut* also occurs. | [CORE] |
| אמונה | ʾemunah | faithfulness, trust, belief; from root א-מ-נ (ʾ-m-n) | faith, trust, faithfulness, reliability | Denotes both the quality of being trustworthy or faithful and the act of believing or trusting. Used in religious, moral, and interpersonal contexts; *ʾemunah* in a person implies they are reliable and honest. The root connects it to *neʾeman* ("faithful, reliable") and *maʾamin* ("believer"). | [CORE] |
| נאמן | neʾeman | faithful, loyal, trustworthy; passive/stative pattern from root א-מ-נ (ʾ-m-n), "one who is trusted" | faithful, loyal, trustworthy, reliable | Describes persons who are dependable and honest in fulfilling obligations or representing facts accurately. Used in legal contexts (*neʾeman le-ʿedut*, "competent/reliable as a witness") and in everyday moral evaluation. Also used as a title, e.g., *neʾeman bayit* ("a trusted household steward"). | [CORE] |
| כנות | kanut | sincerity, honesty; abstract noun from כָּן (*kan*, sincere, honest); root כ-נ-נ or כ-ו-נ | sincerity, honesty, genuineness, candor | Refers to the quality of being sincere or honest in one's expressions, intentions, or conduct, without concealment or pretense. Used in moral and interpersonal evaluation to evaluate whether a person's behavior or statements reflect their true inner state. Example: *medaber be-kanut* ("speaking with sincerity"). Contrasts with *sheqer* (falsehood) and *tsevʿiut* ("hypocrisy") in moral discourse. The adjective *ken* and adverb *be-kannut* ("sincerely, honestly") are closely related. | [CORE] |
| כן | ken | upright, sincere, honest; from root כ-נ-נ or כ-ו-נ | sincere, honest, candid, genuine | Describes a person or statement as straightforward and free from deception. Used in moral evaluation of persons and their speech. Example: *adam ken* ("an honest/sincere person"). Participates in derivations including *kanut* ("sincerity") and *le-hiyot ken* ("to be honest"). | [CORE] |
| שֶׁקֶר | sheqer | falsehood, lie; root ש-ק-ר (sh-q-r) | falsehood, lie, deception, fraud, untruth | The primary Hebrew term for falsehood or lying, and the primary antonym of *ʾemet*, used across moral, legal, religious, and everyday contexts. Appears in the biblical prohibition *midvar sheqer tirḥaq* ("distance yourself from falsehood") and in modern Hebrew to describe lies, false testimony, and fraudulent representations. Also used attributively, as in *ʿed sheqer* ("false witness"). Defines the negative pole against which *ʾemet* is measured. Participates in derivations such as *shakran* ("liar") and *shaqri* ("false, spurious"). | [CORE] |
| זיוף | ziyyuf | forgery, falsification; verbal noun from root ז-י-פ (z-y-f), to falsify, counterfeit | forgery, falsification, counterfeiting, fraud | Refers to the act or product of deliberately falsifying documents, artworks, currency, signatures, or other representations. A standard legal and administrative term. Example: *ziyyuf mismakh* ("document forgery"). Closely related to *mezuyaf* ("forged") and *mezayef* ("forger"). The verb *lezayef* means "to forge" or "to falsify." | [CORE] |
| מזויף | mezuyaf | forged, falsified, counterfeit; Pu'al passive participle from root ז-י-פ (z-y-f) | forged, fake, counterfeit, falsified | The adjectival/participial form describing something that has been falsified or is not genuine. Applied to documents, signatures, artworks, currency, credentials, and identities that have been deliberately made to appear genuine when they are not. Common in legal and journalistic contexts. Example: *teʿudat zehut mezuyefet* ("a forged identity document"). Directly contrasts with *meqori* (original) and *ʾotenti* (authentic). | [CORE] |
| צֶדֶק | tsedeq | justice, righteousness; root צ-ד-ק (ts-d-q), to be right, just | justice, righteousness, rightness | A foundational term in biblical, rabbinic, and modern Hebrew for justice and moral rightness, used in evaluating conduct, judgments, and social arrangements. Used in legal contexts (*mishpat u-tsedeq*, "justice and righteousness") and in evaluating whether an action or judgment is correct or fair. The related verb *tsadaq* means "to be right" or "to be justified." Participates in a large derivational family including *tsaddiq* ("righteous person") and *letsdiq* ("to justify, to vindicate"). Closely related to *tsaddiq* (righteous person) and *tsedaqa* (righteousness, charity). | [CORE] |
| צדיק | tsaddiq | righteous, just person; root צ-ד-ק (ts-d-q); intensive adjectival form | righteous, just, upright | Describes a person whose conduct conforms to moral and religious standards of rightness. A key evaluative term in biblical, rabbinic, and modern Hebrew moral discourse. Can also be used more loosely in modern Hebrew to describe someone who is blameless in a particular situation. | [CORE] |
| ישר | yashar | straight, upright, honest; root י-ש-ר (y-sh-r) | upright, honest, straightforward, just | A moral and evaluative term describing persons and conduct as morally straight, honest, and without deception or deviation. Appears extensively in biblical and rabbinic literature and remains in use in modern Hebrew in moral and legal discourse. Appears in the biblical phrase *ha-yashar be-ʿeynav* ("what is right in his eyes"). Yields derivations such as *yosher* ("uprightness, integrity") and *le-yasher* ("to straighten, to approve"). | [CORE] |
| יושר | yosher | uprightness, integrity, honesty; abstract noun from root י-ש-ר (y-sh-r) | integrity, uprightness, honesty, fairness | Refers to the quality of moral uprightness or integrity in a person's conduct or character. Used in ethical and legal discourse, sometimes approximating "equity" or "fairness." Appears in fixed expressions such as *middat ha-yosher* ("the standard of fairness/equity") and *yosher lev* ("integrity of heart"). Used in modern contract law discourse. Closely related to *yashar* but functions as an abstract quality noun rather than an attributive adjective. Example: *ʾish yosher* ("a man of integrity"). | [CORE] |
| רמאות | ramaʾut | deceit, fraud; abstract noun from root ר-מ-א (r-m-ʾ), to deceive, to cheat | deceit, fraud, cheating, trickery | Denotes the practice of deliberately misleading others, used in moral, legal, and everyday contexts to evaluate conduct as dishonest or fraudulent. Appears in legal discourse concerning commercial fraud and in everyday moral condemnation. The root yields *rammaʾi* ("deceiver, cheat") and *leramot* ("to deceive"). | [CORE] |
| הונאה | honaʾah | deception, fraud; verbal noun from root א-נ-ה in Hif'il pattern, to deceive, to defraud | deception, fraud, swindling | Used in legal and moral contexts to describe deliberate misleading of another person, particularly for material gain. Appears in contract law and consumer protection discourse. Example: *honaʾah be-miqaḥ u-memkar* ("fraud in buying and selling," a classical legal category). Yields *meʾoneh* ("deceiver") and *lehaʾot* ("to deceive"). | [CORE] |
| צביעות | tsevʿiut | hypocrisy, insincerity; from *tsavoaʿ* ("dyed, colored"); abstract noun; "being two-colored, hypocrisy" | hypocrisy, insincerity, two-facedness | Denotes the quality of presenting a false appearance of virtue or sincerity while concealing contrary intentions or conduct. Used in moral evaluation of persons and public figures. Example: *ze tsevʿiut mehuḥatsefet* ("that is blatant hypocrisy"). Contrasts with *kanut* ("sincerity") and *yosher* ("integrity"). | [CORE] |
| תקין | taqin | proper, in order, functioning correctly; root ת-ק-נ (t-q-n), to fix, correct, regulate | proper, correct, in order, functioning correctly, valid | Evaluates whether something is functioning correctly, is in proper order, or conforms to a standard — a machine, a procedure, a document, or conduct. Common in administrative, technical, and legal contexts. In legal and bureaucratic contexts it can indicate that a document or process is formally valid and correct. Implies conformity to a standard or norm rather than moral rightness per se. | [CORE] |
| תקף | taqef | valid, in force; root ת-ק-פ (t-q-p), strength, force, to be strong, valid, in force | valid, in force, effective, legally binding | Used primarily in legal and administrative contexts to describe documents, contracts, licenses, laws, or decisions that are currently in force and legally effective. Contrasts with *lo taqef* (invalid, expired) and *batel* ("null, void"). The noun *toqef* means validity or force. | [CORE] |
| בטל | batel | null, void, invalid; root ב-ט-ל (b-t-l), to be null, cease, be annulled | null, void, invalid, annulled | The standard legal and everyday term for something that is null, void, or without effect. Used in legal discourse (contracts, rulings) and in rabbinic law. The verb *levatel* means "to annul, cancel, nullify." | [CORE] |
| חוקי | ḥuqi | legal, lawful; derived from חוֹק (*ḥoq*, law, statute); root ח-ק-ק (ḥ-q-q) | legal, lawful, legitimate | Evaluates whether an action, document, or status conforms to law. Used in legal and administrative contexts to distinguish what is permitted or valid under law from what is not. Contrasts with *bilti ḥuqi* (illegal, unlawful). | [CORE] |
| לגיטימי | legitimi | legitimate; loanword from Latin/European *legitimus* | legitimate, valid, justified | Used in political, legal, and moral discourse to evaluate whether a claim, authority, action, or representation is justified or valid according to recognized standards. Functions as a direct parallel to English "legitimate" and is common in modern Hebrew public discourse. | [CORE] |
| כשר | kasher | fit, proper, valid; root כ-ש-ר (k-sh-r), fitness, suitability | fit, proper, valid, legitimate, kosher (in religious law) | Evaluates whether something meets the relevant standard of fitness or validity. In religious law, evaluates whether food, objects, or persons meet the required standards of fitness. Used broadly in rabbinic and legal contexts to mean "valid" or "fit," e.g., *ʿed kasher* ("a valid/competent witness"), *get kasher* ("a valid bill of divorce"). In broader modern Hebrew usage, *kasher* can describe any person or thing that is legitimate, proper, or above suspicion. Contrasts directly with *pasul* ("invalid, disqualified"). The noun *kashrut* refers to the state of being fit or valid as well as the dietary system. | [CORE] |
| פסול | pasul | disqualified, invalid, unfit; Qal passive participle from root פ-ס-ל (p-s-l), to disqualify, to hew away, to invalidate | invalid, disqualified, unfit, inadmissible | Evaluates persons, evidence, documents, or ritual objects as disqualified or invalid according to a relevant standard. Used in legal, religious, and general contexts to evaluate something or someone as failing to meet required standards and therefore invalid or inadmissible. Widely used in rabbinic law, e.g., a witness who is *pasul le-ʿedut* ("disqualified from testimony"), and in modern Israeli legal and administrative contexts. Example: *edut pesula* ("inadmissible testimony"). Contrasts directly with *kasher*. | [CORE] |
| סביר | savir | reasonable, plausible; root ס-ב-ר (s-b-r), to think, suppose, consider plausible | reasonable, plausible, credible | Evaluates whether a claim, explanation, or course of action is reasonable or plausible given available evidence or norms. Central in legal discourse, e.g., *ha-ʾadam ha-savir* ("the reasonable person" standard). Also used in everyday contexts to assess whether something makes sense or is believable. The noun *sevirut* denotes reasonableness. | [CORE] |
| מהות | mahut | essence, nature; derived from מָה (*ma*, what) + abstract suffix; "whatness, essence" | essence, nature, substance, what something fundamentally is | A philosophical and general-purpose term for the fundamental nature or defining character of something, used in contexts where one evaluates what something truly or essentially is. Appears in philosophical writing and in educated everyday speech. Example: *mahut ha-davar* ("the essence of the matter"). Participates in the compound *mahuti* ("essential, substantive"). | [CORE] |
| עצם | ʿetsem | bone, essence, self, very; root ע-צ-מ (ʿ-ts-m), strength, selfhood | essence, the very thing itself, substance; (in compounds) the actual, the real | Used in philosophical and legal Hebrew to indicate the essential or intrinsic nature of something, or to emphasize identity. Often appears in the construction *be-ʿetsem* ("in essence, actually") or *ʿetsem ha-davar* ("the very matter itself"). Also functions as a reflexive intensifier. In legal Hebrew, *ʿetsem ha-ʿinyan* means "the substance of the matter." Its use as an essence-term is more contextually determined than *mahut*. | [CORE] |
| דומה | dome | similar, resembling; root ד-מ-ה (d-m-h), to resemble, liken | similar, resembling, like | Evaluates resemblance or likeness between two entities. Used across all registers, including everyday and legal contexts (e.g., evaluating whether a copy resembles an original, or whether cases are analogous). The related noun *dimyon* means "resemblance" or "similarity," and the verb *ledamot* means "to resemble" or "to compare." | [CORE] |
| דמיון | dimyon | resemblance, likeness; from root ד-מ-ה (d-m-h), to resemble, to be like | resemblance, similarity, likeness; (also) imagination | In evaluative contexts, used to assess the degree to which one thing resembles another, relevant to questions of authenticity, imitation, and representation. The same word also means "imagination," which can create ambiguity; context disambiguates. Appears in aesthetic and legal discussions of imitation and copying. | [CORE] |
| דיוק | diyyuq | precision, exactness; verbal noun from root ד-י-ק (d-y-q), fineness, exactness | precision, accuracy, exactness | Refers to the quality of being exact or precise in a statement, measurement, or representation. Used in scientific, legal, scholarly, and journalistic contexts to evaluate how closely something corresponds to what it describes. Common expressions include *be-diyyuq* ("precisely, exactly") and *ḥoser diyyuq* ("lack of precision, inaccuracy"). The verb *ledayeq* means "to be precise" or "to examine closely." Closely related to *meduyaq* ("accurate, precise"). | [CORE] |
| הגון | hagun | decent, proper, fitting; root ה-ג-נ (h-g-n), related to propriety; etymology debated | decent, proper, respectable, fitting, fair | Evaluates persons, conduct, or offers as conforming to standards of decency, fairness, and propriety. Common in everyday speech and in legal or commercial contexts. Example: *meḥir hagun* ("a fair price"). Also used to evaluate moral character. Contrasts with *lo hagun* (improper, indecent, not fitting), which is also a common fixed expression. | [CORE] |
| לא הגון | lo hagun | not decent, not fitting; negation of *hagun* | improper, indecent, unfair, not right | A fixed negative evaluative expression used to describe conduct, treatment, or persons that fall below standards of decency or fairness. Extremely common in everyday moral and social evaluation. Functions as a conventionalized expression rather than a free negation. | [CORE] |
| ספק | safek | doubt, uncertainty; root ס-פ-ק (s-p-q) | doubt, uncertainty, question | Used in legal, religious, and everyday contexts to indicate that the truth, validity, or identity of something is uncertain or in question. In halakhic discourse, *safek* triggers specific rules for resolving uncertainty. In everyday usage, *be-li safek* ("without doubt") and *yesh safek* ("there is doubt") are common evaluative phrases. | [CORE] |
| חיקוי | ḥiqquy | imitation, mimicry; verbal noun from root ח-ק-ה (ḥ-q-h), to imitate, to copy | imitation, mimicry, copy | Refers to the act or product of imitating something, used in aesthetic, legal, and everyday contexts to evaluate whether something is original or merely a copy. Relevant to questions of authenticity and resemblance. Example: *ḥiqquy zol* ("a cheap imitation"). Contrasts with *meqori* ("original") and relates to *mezuyaf* when the imitation is deceptive. | [CORE] |
| עדות | ʿedut | testimony, witness; from root ע-ד-ה/ע-ו-ד (ʿ-d-h/ʿ-w-d) | testimony, evidence, witness | The standard term for testimony given by a witness in legal or quasi-legal contexts, where its truthfulness and reliability are subject to evaluation. Central to both biblical law and modern Israeli legal procedure. Examples: *ʿedut sheqer* ("false testimony") and *ʿedut neʾemenet* ("reliable testimony"). Participates in derivations including *ʿed* ("witness") and *lehaʿid* ("to testify"). | [CORE] |
| זהה | zehe | identical, the same; from root ז-ה-ה or related to *ze* ("this"); denotes identity/sameness | identical, the same | Evaluates whether two things are identical or the same. Used in legal, scientific, and everyday contexts. The noun *zahut* means "identity" (both personal identity and logical identity/sameness). | [CORE] |
| אֱמוּנָה / אמונה | ʾemunah | faithfulness, trust, belief; from root א-מ-נ + nominal pattern *ʾeCuCa* + feminine suffix -ah | faith, belief, faithfulness, trust | One of the most central terms in Hebrew religious and moral discourse, referring to the quality of trusting in God, a person, or a principle, and to the state of being faithful. Used in theological contexts (*ʾemuna be-ʾelohim*, faith in God), in moral evaluation (*ʾish ʾemuna*, a man of faith/faithfulness), and in the fixed phrase *ʾemet ve-ʾemuna* (truth and faithfulness). Also used in modern Hebrew for religious belief more broadly. Used across biblical, rabbinic, and modern contexts. | [CORE] |
| אֱמוּן / אמון | ʾemun / ʾimun | trust, confidence, reliance; also training, practice; root א-מ-נ + nominal pattern; also analyzed as Pi'el verbal noun pattern | trust, confidence, reliance; also training, practice | Used in two distinct senses: (a) interpersonal or institutional trust, e.g., *ʾimun ha-tsibur* ("public trust/confidence"), *ʾemun ha-tsibbur* ("public trust"); and (b) professional or physical training, e.g., *ʾimun tsvaʾi* ("military training"). Context disambiguates. Common in political and social discourse. Also appears in the phrase *ʾish ʾemun* (a trusted person, a confidant). Slightly more abstract and institutional than *ʾemuna*. | [CORE] |
| נֶאֱמָן / נאמן | neʾeman | faithful, loyal, trustworthy, reliable; root א-מ-נ, Nif'al participle | faithful, loyal, trustworthy, reliable; also trustee, fiduciary (in legal contexts) | Used to describe persons who are loyal and can be trusted — a faithful friend, a loyal employee, a reliable witness. Common in both everyday and formal Hebrew. Appears in fixed phrases such as *neʾeman le-* (faithful/loyal to) and *neʾeman la-ʾemet* (faithful to the truth). Also used as a title or form of address in some religious contexts. In legal and financial contexts, *neʾeman* denotes a trustee or fiduciary — a person entrusted with managing assets or interests on behalf of another. Standard legal terminology. | [CORE] |
| נֶאֱמָנוּת / נאמנות | neʾemanut | loyalty, faithfulness, fidelity, trustworthiness; root א-מ-נ, Nif'al nominal form + *-ut* suffix | loyalty, faithfulness, fidelity, trustworthiness; also trust (legal), fiduciary relationship, trusteeship | The abstract noun denoting the quality of being loyal or faithful. Used in moral, political, and legal discourse to evaluate whether a person or institution has maintained fidelity to a commitment, person, or principle. Common in discussions of political loyalty, marital fidelity, and professional integrity. In legal contexts, *neʾemanut* denotes a trust or fiduciary arrangement. Standard in Israeli property and financial law. | [CORE] |
| הֶאֱמִין / האמין | heʾemin | believed, trusted; root א-מ-נ, Hif'il perfect 3ms | believed, trusted (verb: to believe, to trust) | The standard verb for "to believe" in Hebrew, used in both religious contexts (believing in God) and everyday epistemic contexts (believing a person, believing a claim). The infinitive *lehaʾamin* is extremely common. Takes the preposition *be-* (*lehaʾamin be-*, to believe in) or *le-* (*lehaʾamin le-*, to believe someone). "אני מאמין לך" ("I believe you") is a common everyday expression. | [CORE] |
| אֵמוּן / אמון (training sense) | ʾemun (training sense) | training, apprenticeship, upbringing; root א-מ-נ + nominal pattern | training, apprenticeship, upbringing | Used to describe the process of training or raising someone — an apprentice, a ward, or a trainee. Appears in the phrase *ben ʾemun* (a ward, a foster child) and in contexts of professional training. This is a distinct semantic branch of the root from the trust/belief cluster. | [CORE] |
| אוֹמֵן / אומן | ʾomen | trainer, tutor, foster father, guardian; root א-מ-נ, Qal active participle | trainer, tutor, foster father, guardian | Used in biblical and literary Hebrew to describe a person who raises or trains another — a guardian, tutor, or foster parent. Appears in the biblical narrative of Mordecai as the *ʾomen* of Esther. Less common in everyday modern Hebrew but retained in literary and religious registers. | [MARGINAL] |
| אוֹמֶנֶת / אומנת | ʾomenet | nurse, nanny, foster mother, guardian; root א-מ-נ, Qal active participle, feminine form | nurse, nanny, foster mother, guardian | The feminine counterpart of *ʾomen*, used in biblical and literary Hebrew for a woman who raises or nurses a child. Appears in biblical narrative (e.g., the nurse of the infant Joash). Retained in literary and religious registers; less common in everyday modern Hebrew. | [MARGINAL] |
| מַאֲמִין / מאמין | maʾamin | believer, one who believes; trusting; root א-מ-נ, Hif'il active participle | believer, one who believes; trusting | Used to describe a person who holds religious belief or who believes a particular claim. In religious discourse, *maʾamin* denotes a believer in God or in a religious doctrine. In everyday discourse, it can describe someone who believes a particular person or claim, e.g., *ʾani maʾamin she-hu tsodeq* ("I believe he is right"). The plural *maʾaminim* is common in religious contexts. Used as both a verbal participle ("I believe") and a noun ("a believer"). | [CORE] |
| אֲמָנָה / אמנה | ʾamana / ʾamanaʾh | agreement, covenant, charter, compact; root א-מ-נ + nominal pattern *ʾaCaCa* + feminine suffix | agreement, covenant, charter, compact | Used in legal, political, and international contexts to describe a formal agreement or charter between parties. | Group 1 — Expressions used to evaluate whether a statement or claim is correct or true | These expressions are used in everyday spoken Hebrew and in journalistic and analytical writing to confirm or deny that a statement, answer, or fact is correct. | Cognition-evaluating terms in epistemological argument | These terms are used in Sanskrit philosophical literature — primarily Nyāya, Mīmāṃsā, and Buddhist epistemology — to assess whether a given cognitive episode accurately apprehends the object it is directed at. They appear in technical discussions of the structure of knowledge, the causes of error, and the distinction between reliable and unreliable cognitive episodes. They are regularly contrasted with one another as positive and negative poles of the same evaluative dimension. | प्रमा / *pramā*; अप्रमा / *apramā*; यथार्थज्ञान / *yathārthajñāna*; भ्रम / *bhrama*; विपर्यय / *viparyaya*; भ्रमज्ञान / *bhramajñāna*; मिथ्याज्ञान / *mithyājñāna*; भ्रमो न प्रमा / *bhramo na pramā*; विपर्ययो न प्रमा / *viparyayo na pramā*; भ्रान्ति / *bhrānti*; भ्रान्त / *bhrānta*; भ्रान्तिज्ञान / *bhrānti-jñāna*; भ्रामक / *bhrāmaka*; विपर्यस्त / *viparyasta*; मिथ्यादृष्टि / *mithyā-dṛṣṭi*; अविसंवादिन् / *avisaṃvādin*; असत्ख्याति / *asatkhyāti*; विपर्ययो मिथ्याज्ञानम् / *viparyayo mithyājñānam*; मिथ्याज्ञानं निवर्तते सम्यग्ज्ञानेन / *mithyājñānaṃ nivartate samyag-jñānena*; रज्जौ सर्पभ्रान्तिः / *rajjau sarpa-bhrāntiḥ*; भ्रान्तिः निवर्तते / *bhrāntiḥ nivartate*; बाधेन भ्रान्तिः निवर्तते / *bādhena bhrāntiḥ nivartate*; बाधित / *bādhita*; बाधा / *bādhā* | मिथ्याज्ञान / *mithyājñāna* (also Group 5, carries Advaita Vedānta ontological connotations); भ्रम / *bhrama* and विपर्यय / *viparyaya* (near-synonyms across different school vocabularies); भ्रान्ति / *bhrānti* (near-synonym of *bhrama*) | *Bhrama* and *viparyaya* are near-synonyms in function but belong to different school vocabularies; *bhrama* is the standard Nyāya term, *viparyaya* the standard Sāṃkhya-Yoga term. *Bhrānti* is a near-synonym of *bhrama* emphasizing the state of being in error. *Mithyājñāna* carries additional Advaita Vedānta connotations about the ontological status of the object, not only the accuracy of the cognition. *Apramā* is the most technically neutral negation. *Avisaṃvādin* is a Buddhist *pramāṇa*-theory term. |
| Source-evaluating terms in epistemological argument | These terms are used to assess not the cognition itself but the means, source, or procedure by which it is produced. They appear in debates across all major Sanskrit philosophical schools about which sources of knowledge count as authoritative and why. The central question is not whether a particular cognition is accurate but whether the *means* by which it was arrived at is reliable. The central term *pramāṇa* generates a large cluster of derived expressions that evaluate sources as genuine, spurious, absent, or contested. | प्रमाण / *pramāṇa*; प्रामाण्य / *prāmāṇya*; अप्रामाण्य / *aprāmāṇya*; स्वतःप्रामाण्य / *svataḥprāmāṇya*; परतःप्रामाण्य / *parataḥprāmāṇya*; प्रमाणाभास / *pramāṇābhāsa*; हेत्वाभास / *hetvābhāsa*; प्रमाणेन सिद्धम् / *pramāṇena siddham*; प्रमाणाभावात् / *pramāṇābhāvāt*; प्रमाणं नास्ति / *pramāṇaṃ nāsti*; प्रमाणविरुद्ध / *pramāṇaviruddha*; प्रमाणसिद्ध / *pramāṇasiddha*; अनुमान / *anumāna*; अनुमिति / *anumiti*; उपमान / *upamāna*; प्रामाणिक / *prāmāṇika*; अप्रमाण / *apramāṇa*; अप्रामाणिक / *aprāmāṇika*; प्रमाणभूत / *pramāṇabhūta*; प्रमाणता / *pramāṇatā*; प्रमातृ / *pramātṛ*; प्रमेय / *prameya*; वेदः प्रमाणम् / *vedaḥ pramāṇam*; प्रमाणं किम्? / *pramāṇaṃ kim?*; न तत्र प्रमाणम् अस्ति / *na tatra pramāṇam asti*; प्रमायाः करणं प्रमाणम् / *pramāyāḥ karaṇaṃ pramāṇam*; हेत्वाभासो न हेतुः / *hetvābhāso na hetuḥ* | प्रमाण / *pramāṇa* (also Group 1, as the source that produces *pramā*); हेत्वाभास / *hetvābhāsa* (a specific application of the *ābhāsa* pattern to inferential reasoning) | The *svataḥ/parataḥ* pair marks a specific intra-school debate about the locus of validity-conferring conditions. *Hetvābhāsa* is a specialized application of the *ābhāsa* (semblance) pattern to the specific case of inferential reasoning. *Pramāṇābhāsa* is the more general term for spurious epistemic sources. This group is closely related to Group 1 but is distinct: Group 1 terms evaluate individual cognitions or statements, while Group 2 terms evaluate the *sources and methods* that generate cognitions. The two groups interact: a cognition is *pramā* (Group 1) when it results from a *pramāṇa* (Group 2). |
| Speech-evaluating terms in ethical and legal contexts | These terms are used in Dharmaśāstra, epic literature, and legal contexts to evaluate utterances, testimony, and speech acts as truthful, false, or wrongful. The evaluative dimension here is primarily moral and legal rather than epistemological. | सत्य / *satya*; असत्य / *asatya*; अनृत / *anṛta*; तथ्य / *tathya*; सत्यवादिन् / *satyavādin*; असत्यवादिन् / *asatyavādin*; मिथ्यावादिन् / *mithyāvādin*; सत्यवचन / *satyavacana*; असत्यवचन / *asatyavacana*; अनृतवचन / *anṛtavacana*; असत्यभाषण / *asatya-bhāṣaṇa*; अनृतभाषिन् / *anṛta-bhāṣin*; सत्यवाक्य / *satya-vākya*; सत्यसंध / *satyasaṃdha*; सत्यं वद / *satyaṃ vada*; सत्यं ब्रूयात् / *satyaṃ brūyāt*; असत्यं न वदेत् / *asatyaṃ na vadet*; अनृतं न वदेत् / *anṛtaṃ na vadet*; तथ्यं वदति / *tathyaṃ vadati*; असत्यं पापम् / *asatyaṃ pāpam*; असत्यं वदति / *asatyaṃ vadati*; मिथ्या न वदेत् / *mithyā na vadet*; सत्यं नास्ति परो धर्मः / *satyaṃ nāsti paro dharmaḥ*; सत्यं परं धर्मः / *satyaṃ paraṃ dharmaḥ* | सत्य / *satya* (also Groups 4, 5, 6); अनृत / *anṛta* (older Vedic term with cosmological connotations, overlapping with Group 5); तथ्य / *tathya* (also Group 4); मिथ्यावादिन् / *mithyāvādin* (overlapping with Group 1) | *Satya* and *asatya* are the most widely used pair in post-Vedic prose. *Anṛta* is the older Vedic term and carries cosmological connotations that *asatya* does not. *Tathya* is more restricted to factual accuracy in legal and narrative contexts and lacks the moral weight of *satya*. | Reality-correspondence terms in philosophical and general prose | These terms are used to assess whether a description, property, or characterization pertains to how things actually are, as opposed to how they appear, are conventionally described, or are merely named. They appear in philosophical argument when distinguishing genuine from apparent or conventional properties, and in general prose when asserting that an account is accurate to the facts. They are regularly contrasted with terms for appearance, convention, or mere verbal designation. | वास्तव / *vāstava*; वस्तु / *vastu*; यथार्थ / *yathārtha*; तथ्य / *tathya*; वस्तुतः / *vastutaḥ*; वास्तवतः / *vāstavataḥ*; वस्तुस्थिति / *vastusthiti*; वस्तुनि यथावत् ज्ञानम् / *vastuni yathāvat jñānam*; वस्तु न शब्दाधीनम् / *vastu na śabdādhīnam*; वस्तुबलात् / *vastubalaāt*; वास्तविक / *vāstavika*; वस्तुस्वभाव / *vastusvabhāva*; वस्तुतन्त्र / *vastu-tantra*; वस्तुसत् / *vastu-sat*; यथार्थता / *yathārthatā*; आभासमात्रम् न वस्तु / *ābhāsamātram na vastu* | वस्तु / *vastu* (also Group 5); यथार्थ / *yathārtha* (also Group 1); तथ्य / *tathya* (also Group 3) | *Vastu* and *vāstava* are closely related, with *vastu* being the noun (the real thing) and *vāstava* the adjective (pertaining to the real thing). *Yathārtha* emphasizes the correspondence relation between a description and its object, while *vastu*/*vāstava* emphasize the ontological status of the object itself. *Tathya* overlaps with this group but is more restricted to factual accuracy in testimony and narrative. |

In moral contexts it can indicate rightness of action. | [CORE] |
| σωστός | sostós | from σώζω (to save, preserve); "preserved intact," hence "correct, sound" | correct, right, proper, accurate, sound | The most common colloquial term for "correct" in modern Greek, used of answers, behavior, persons, procedures, and objects. Overlaps with ορθός but is more frequent in informal registers. Η σωστή απάντηση means "the correct answer." | [CORE] |
| λανθασμένος | lanthazmenos | past participle of λανθάνομαι (to be mistaken, to err) | wrong, mistaken, erroneous, incorrect | Applied to beliefs, statements, calculations, and actions to indicate that they are in error. Common in everyday and educational contexts as the standard antonym of σωστός. | [CORE] |
| έγκυρος | éngiros | from ἐν- (in) + κῦρος (authority, validity); "having authority" | valid, authoritative, reliable, credible, legitimate | Used in legal, administrative, and epistemic contexts to indicate that a document, argument, decision, or source carries recognized authority or meets formal requirements. A passport, contract, or election may be described as έγκυρος. Contrasts with άκυρος ("invalid, null"). Έγκυρο συμβόλαιο means "valid contract." | [CORE] |
| νόμιμος | nómimos | from νόμος (law); "according to law" | legal, lawful, legitimate | Indicates conformity with legal norms or established rules. Applied to persons, actions, and documents. Contrasts with παράνομος (illegal). | [CORE] |
| αξιόπιστος | aksiópistos | ἄξιος (worthy) + πίστις (trust, faith); "worthy of trust" | reliable, trustworthy, credible | Applied to persons, sources, institutions, and testimonies to indicate that they merit confidence and can be trusted or believed. Frequently used in journalistic and legal contexts when evaluating the credibility of witnesses or information sources. Αξιόπιστη πηγή means "reliable source." | [CORE] |
| αναξιόπιστος | anaksiópistos | privative ἀν- + αξιόπιστος; "not worthy of trust" | unreliable, untrustworthy, incredible | The direct negation of αξιόπιστος, applied to persons, sources, and claims. Used in evaluative contexts where credibility is at issue. | [CORE] |
| αξιόλογος | aksiólogos | ἄξιος (worthy) + λόγος (word, account, reason); "worthy of account" | noteworthy, significant, considerable, creditable, of merit | Used to evaluate persons, achievements, or works as deserving recognition or serious consideration. Applied to persons, works, or achievements to indicate that they are genuinely worthy of attention or merit. Carries a positive evaluative force and appears in both formal and informal registers, as well as academic and critical registers. | [CORE] |
| νόθος | nóthos | "of illegitimate birth," hence "spurious, counterfeit" | spurious, illegitimate, counterfeit, false, adulterated | Historically used of illegitimate children; extended to texts, documents, and objects to indicate that they are not what they claim to be. Used in philological and legal contexts (e.g., a νόθο κείμενο is a text of doubtful authenticity). In textual criticism, applied to works falsely attributed to an author. | [CORE] |
| πλαστός | plastós | from πλάσσω / πλάθω (to mold, fabricate); "fabricated, molded" | forged, counterfeit, fake, fabricated | Applied to documents, signatures, currency, and identities to indicate deliberate falsification. Implies deliberate fabrication. Πλαστή ταυτότητα is a forged identity document; πλαστό διαβατήριο means "forged passport." Commonly used in legal and criminal contexts. | [CORE] |
| ψεύτικος | psévtikos / pséftikos | from ψεύτης (liar) / ψεύδος (falsehood, lie); "of the nature of a lie, false" | false, fake, counterfeit, lying | A common colloquial adjective applied to objects, persons, and statements to indicate that they are not genuine or truthful. Less formal than πλαστός and broader in application. Contrasts with αληθινός and γνήσιος in everyday speech. | [CORE] |
| ψευδής | psevdís | from ψεύδος (falsehood); "characterized by falsehood" | false, untrue, mendacious, lying, spurious | More formal than ψεύτικος; used of statements, testimony, documents, and representations in legal and philosophical contexts to indicate falsity or deceptiveness. A ψευδής κατάθεση is false testimony. Participates in compounds such as ψευδώνυμο (pseudonym). | [CORE] |
| ψεύδος | psévdos | "falsehood, lie" | falsehood, lie, untruth | The primary noun for a falsehood or lie, used in philosophical, legal, and everyday contexts. Participates in a large derivational family: ψεύτης (liar), ψεύδομαι (to lie), ψευδής (false). Also appears in the compound ψευδώνυμο and in compounds such as ψευδοεπιστήμη ("pseudoscience"). In everyday speech the plural ψέματα is the colloquial form (λέω ψέματα, "I tell lies"). | [CORE] |
| αμφίβολος | amfívolos | ἀμφί (on both sides) + βάλλω (to throw); "thrown both ways, doubtful" | doubtful, dubious, questionable, ambiguous | Applied to persons, situations, claims, and cases whose reliability, truth, or quality is in question or uncertain. An αμφίβολη υπόθεση is a dubious case or affair. Used in both everyday and formal registers. | [CORE] |
| αμφισβητήσιμος | amfisvitiísimos | from αμφισβητώ (to dispute, contest); "disputable, contestable" | disputable, contestable, questionable, debatable | Applied to claims, titles, rights, and facts that are open to challenge or have not been definitively established. More formal than αμφίβολος and more specifically tied to the possibility of active contestation. Frequently used in legal and academic contexts to flag that a proposition or right is not settled. | [CORE] |
| αμφισβητώ | amfisviтó | ἀμφί (on both sides) + σβητός; conventionally "to dispute, contest" | to dispute, to contest, to challenge, to question | A verb used to indicate that a claim, right, or fact is being actively challenged. Used in legal proceedings (αμφισβητώ μια κατάθεση) and in everyday argument. Productive derivational base for αμφισβήτηση, αμφισβητήσιμος. | [CORE] |
| αδιαμφισβήτητος | adiamfisvitiitos | ἀ- (privative) + διαμφισβητέω (to dispute thoroughly); "not disputable" | indisputable, unquestionable, undeniable | Applied to facts, rights, and truths that are held to be beyond reasonable challenge. Used for emphasis in legal, rhetorical, and everyday contexts. | [CORE] |
| αποδεδειγμένος | apodedeignménos | perfect passive participle of ἀποδείκνυμι (to demonstrate, prove); "having been demonstrated" | proven, demonstrated, established | Applied to facts, claims, and propositions that have been shown to be true through evidence or argument. Used in legal, scientific, and everyday contexts. | [CORE] |
| τεκμηριωμένος | tekmirio̱ménos | from τεκμήριον (evidence, proof); "supported by evidence" | documented, evidenced, substantiated | Applied to claims, arguments, and positions that are backed by concrete evidence or documentation. Common in journalistic, academic, and legal registers. | [CORE] |
| επαληθεύω | epalithévo | ἐπί (upon, toward) + αληθεύω (to be true); "to verify, confirm as true" | to verify, to confirm, to validate, to corroborate | Used in scientific, journalistic, and administrative contexts to indicate the process of checking whether a claim, result, or document is accurate or genuine. The noun επαλήθευση is used for the act of verification. | [CORE] |
| επαλήθευση | epalíthefsi | nominal form of επαληθεύω; "the act of verifying" | verification, confirmation, validation | Used in scientific, legal, and administrative contexts to refer to the process or result of checking accuracy or truth. Appears in formal documents and procedures. | [CORE] |
| διαψεύδω | diapsévdo | διά (through, thoroughly) + ψεύδω (to deceive, to falsify); "to refute, to give the lie to" | to refute, to deny, to disprove, to contradict | Used when a claim, rumor, or allegation is officially or demonstrably shown to be false. Common in journalistic and official contexts (e.g., η κυβέρνηση διέψευσε τις φήμες, "the government denied/refuted the rumors"). | [CORE] |
| διαπίστωση | diapístoси | from διαπιστώνω (to ascertain, establish); "the act of ascertaining" | finding, ascertainment, determination, observation | Used to refer to the result of an investigation or observation that establishes a fact. Common in official reports, medical contexts, and everyday speech when someone states what they have found to be the case. | [CORE] |
| τεκμήριο | tekmírio | from τεκμαίρομαι (to infer, judge by signs); "sign, proof, evidence" | evidence, proof, indication, token | Used in legal and argumentative contexts to refer to a piece of evidence or an indicator that supports a conclusion. A τεκμήριο is typically indirect evidence from which a fact is inferred, distinguishing it from direct proof. | [CORE] |
| απόδειξη | apódhiksi | from αποδεικνύω (to demonstrate, prove); "demonstration, proof" | proof, evidence, receipt, demonstration | Used in logical, legal, and everyday contexts to refer to something that proves or demonstrates a claim. In commercial contexts it also means "receipt." The dual usage reflects the general sense of something that establishes a fact. | [CORE] |
| εικονικός | eikonikós / ikonikós | from εικόνα / εἰκών (image, icon); "of or like an image" | simulated, virtual, nominal, figurative; also: iconic | In modern usage, applied to simulated or nominal states of affairs (e.g., εικονική πραγματικότητα = virtual reality). Can also mean "nominal" or "token" in legal and financial contexts, indicating something that resembles but is not the real thing. In legal contexts, an εικονική πράξη is a sham transaction. The evaluative force is that something appears to be what it is not. | [CORE] |
| φαινομενικός | fenomenikós | from φαινόμενον (that which appears); "of or pertaining to appearance" | apparent, seeming, ostensible | Applied to qualities or states that appear to be the case but may not correspond to underlying reality. Φαινομενική επιτυχία means "apparent success." | [CORE] |
| ουσιαστικός | usiástikos / ussiastikós | from οὐσία (essence, substance, being); "of or pertaining to essence" | essential, substantive, real, fundamental, material | Used to distinguish what is genuinely or fundamentally the case from what is merely formal or superficial. In legal contexts, ουσιαστικό δίκαιο means "substantive law" as opposed to procedural law. Also used in everyday speech to mean "real" or "meaningful." Ουσιαστική διαφορά means "a substantive difference." | [CORE] |
| ουσία | ussía | from εἶναι (to be); "being, essence, substance" | essence, substance, matter, gist | Used in philosophical contexts for the fundamental nature of a thing, and in everyday contexts for the essential point or substance of a matter (e.g., η ουσία του ζητήματος, "the substance/gist of the matter"). Also used in legal contexts for "substance" as opposed to form. | [CORE] |
| τυπικός | tipikós | from τύπος (type, form, stamp); "of or pertaining to form or type" | formal, nominal, typical, perfunctory | Often used in contrast to ουσιαστικός to indicate that something satisfies formal requirements without genuine substance. Τυπική συμμόρφωση means "formal compliance." | [CORE] |
| κατ' ουσίαν | kat' usían | κατά (according to, in respect of) + οὐσία (essence); "in respect of essence" | essentially, substantially, in substance | A fixed prepositional expression used to indicate that something is true or the case at the level of substance or essence, as opposed to mere form. Common in legal and philosophical discourse. | [CORE] |
| ομοιότητα | omióтita | from όμοιος (similar, like); "likeness, resemblance" | resemblance, similarity, likeness | Used to describe the degree to which one thing resembles another, relevant in aesthetic evaluation (resemblance of a portrait to its subject) and in legal contexts (resemblance of a trademark to another). Participates in evaluative judgments about representation. | [CORE] |
| αντίγραφο | andígrafo | ἀντί (against, in place of) + γράφω (to write); "written in place of" | copy, reproduction, transcript | Used of documents, artworks, and files to indicate that something is a reproduction rather than the original. The distinction between αντίγραφο and πρωτότυπο (original) is central to legal and archival evaluation of authenticity. | [CORE] |
| πρωτότυπο | protótipo | πρῶτος (first) + τύπος (type, impression); "first impression, original" | original, prototype | Used to designate the original version of a document, artwork, or text as opposed to copies or translations. In aesthetic and legal contexts, the πρωτότυπο carries special authority or value. | [CORE] |
| παραποίηση | parapiísi | from παραποιώ (to alter, falsify); "alteration, falsification" | falsification, adulteration, distortion, tampering | Used in legal and everyday contexts to refer to the deliberate alteration of a document, substance, or account so as to misrepresent it. A παραποίηση εγγράφου is the falsification of a document, a criminal offense. | [CORE] |
| δήθεν | díthен | from δή (indeed, just) + θεν (suffix of origin/manner); "supposedly, allegedly" | supposedly, allegedly, so-called, ostensibly | A particle or adverb expressing skepticism or irony about a claim — that something is presented as being the case but the speaker doubts it. Frequently used with scare-quote force in everyday speech. | [CORE] |
| τάχα | tácha | originally "quickly, perhaps"; in modern usage, "supposedly, as if" | supposedly, allegedly, as if, ostensibly | Used colloquially to cast doubt on a claim or to indicate that something is presented as true but is not believed by the speaker. Often interchangeable with δήθεν in informal registers, though with slightly different pragmatic nuances. | [CORE] |
| φερόμενος ως | ferómenos os | present participle of φέρω (to carry, bear) + ως (as); "being carried/presented as" | alleged, purported, so-called, presented as | A fixed participial expression used in legal, journalistic, and formal contexts to indicate that something is described or presented as having a certain identity or status without that status being confirmed (e.g., φερόμενος ως ιδιοκτήτης, "the purported owner"). | [CORE] |
| κατά φαινόμενον | katá fenómenon | κατά (according to) + φαινόμενον (appearance); "according to appearance" | apparently, ostensibly, in appearance | A fixed prepositional expression contrasting with κατ' ουσίαν, used to indicate that something holds only at the level of appearance. Found in philosophical and formal registers. | [MARGINAL] |
| εικαζόμενος | eikazómenos / ikazómenos | present passive participle of εἰκάζω (to conjecture, liken); "conjectured, supposed" | alleged, supposed, presumed, putative, conjectured | Used in legal and journalistic contexts to describe a person or fact whose status has not been established (e.g., ο εικαζόμενος δράστης, "the alleged perpetrator"). Marks epistemic reservation about a claim. | [MARGINAL] |
| εικός | ikós | from ἔοικα (to seem, resemble); "that which seems likely, probable" | probable, likely, plausible, verisimilar | Found primarily in classical and formal philosophical registers to indicate what is probable or plausible as opposed to what is certain or demonstrated. Less common in contemporary everyday Greek but retained in set expressions and academic writing. | [MARGINAL] |
| αναληθής | analithís | ἀν- (privative) + αληθής; "not true" | untrue, false | A formal or literary negation of αληθής, used in philosophical and written contexts. Less common in everyday speech than ψευδής; tends to appear in contexts where the negation of truth-value is being discussed explicitly. | [MARGINAL] |
| κίβδηλος | kívdhilos / kívdilos | "adulterated, counterfeit" (of coins originally); "base, spurious" | counterfeit, spurious, base, debased, adulterated | Originally applied to debased or counterfeit coinage; extended metaphorically to persons, arguments, and values considered inauthentic or morally debased. Used in formal, literary, and philosophical registers to describe something that appears genuine but is not. Less common in everyday Modern Greek; more frequent in written and elevated registers than πλαστός or ψεύτικος. | [MARGINAL] |
| εικαστικός | eikastikós | from εικάζω (to represent by likeness, to conjecture); "of or pertaining to representation by likeness" | visual (arts), representational, figurative | In Modern Greek, primarily used in the fixed expression εικαστικές τέχνες ("visual/plastic arts"), referring to arts that produce visible representations. The term carries the sense of arts concerned with likeness and representation, though its evaluative dimension (resemblance, fidelity of representation) is more prominent in older or technical usage. | [MARGINAL] |
| αλήθεια (Root 1, anchor) | alíthia | αληθ- (truth) + -εια (abstract noun suffix); "the state of being unconcealed" | truth, truthfulness | The primary noun for truth in all registers. Already listed in P1; included here as the base form for the expansion. | [CORE] |
| αληθής (Root 1, anchor) | alithís | αληθ- (truth) + -ής (adjectival suffix) | true, truthful | Base adjective for truth-value; already in P1. Included as anchor form. | [CORE] |
| αληθινός (Root 1, anchor) | alithinós | αληθ- (truth) + -ινός (adjectival suffix indicating nature or material) | real, genuine, true | Already in P1. Included as anchor form. | [CORE] |
| αληθεύω | alithévo | αληθ- (truth) + -εύω (verbal suffix); "to be truthful, to tell the truth" | to speak the truth, to be truthful, to be accurate | Used in philosophical, literary, and formal registers to describe the act of telling the truth or being in a state of truthfulness. Less common in everyday speech than λέω την αλήθεια. Αληθεύει ότι… means "it is true that…" in formal writing. | [CORE] |
| επαληθεύω (Root 1) | epalithévo | επί (upon, further) + αληθ- (truth) + -εύω (verbal suffix) | to verify, to confirm, to validate | Already in P1. Included here as a derived verbal form. | [CORE] |
| επαλήθευση (Root 1) | epalíthefsi | επί + αληθ- + -ευση (verbal noun suffix) | verification, confirmation, validation | The noun corresponding to επαληθεύω. Used in scientific, administrative, journalistic, and legal contexts to refer to the process or act of verifying a claim, result, or document. | [CORE] |
| επαληθεύσιμος | epalithéfsimos | επαληθεύω (to verify) + -σιμος (adjectival suffix indicating possibility); "capable of being verified" | verifiable | Used in scientific, philosophical, and journalistic contexts to describe claims or hypotheses that can in principle be checked against evidence. Related to the concept of falsifiability in philosophy of science. | [CORE] |
| αληθοφανής | alithofanís | αληθο- (truth-) + φαίνομαι (to appear) + -ής (adjectival suffix); "appearing true" | verisimilar, plausible, lifelike, credible, truth-seeming | Applied to narratives, arguments, and representations that have the appearance of truth or reality without necessarily being true. Used in literary criticism, rhetoric, and philosophical discussion of probability, and in everyday evaluation of stories or claims. | [CORE] |
| αληθοφάνεια | alithofánia | αληθο- (truth-) + φαίνομαι (to appear) + -εια (abstract noun suffix); "the quality of appearing true" | verisimilitude, plausibility, appearance of truth | Used in literary criticism, rhetoric, and philosophy to describe the quality of appearing true or lifelike, without necessarily being true. Applied to narrative, argument, and representation. Corresponds to the classical concept of verisimilitude. Η αληθοφάνεια ενός μυθιστορήματος means "the verisimilitude of a novel." | [CORE] |
| αληθοφάνεια αφήγησης | alithofánia afígisis | αληθοφάνεια (verisimilitude) + αφήγηση (narration) | narrative verisimilitude | A fixed collocation used in literary theory and narratology to refer to the quality of a narrative that makes it seem true or realistic. Common in academic literary criticism and rhetoric. | [CORE] |
| αληθοφανής αφήγηση | alithofanís afígisi | αληθοφανής (verisimilar) + αφήγηση (narration) | verisimilar narrative, plausible account | Used in literary theory and narratology to describe a narrative that achieves the effect of reality or truth. Common in academic literary criticism and rhetoric. | [CORE] |
| αληθινά | alithiná | αληθινός (true, genuine) + -α (adverbial suffix); "truly, genuinely" | truly, really, genuinely | Common adverbial form used in everyday speech to intensify or affirm the truth of a statement. Also used as a discourse marker of sincerity. "Αληθινά δεν το ήξερα" = "I truly didn't know." | [CORE] |
| αληθώς | alithós | αληθ- (truth) + -ώς (adverbial suffix) | truly, verily, in truth | A formal or archaic adverb used in religious, liturgical, and elevated literary contexts. Appears in the Orthodox liturgical response Αληθώς ανέστη ("He is truly risen"). | [CORE] |
| Αληθώς ανέστη | Alithós anésti | αληθώς (truly) + ανέστη (he rose, aorist of ανίσταμαι) | He is truly risen | The liturgical response in the Greek Orthodox Easter service, spoken in reply to Χριστός ανέστη ("Christ is risen"). A fixed religious formula. | [CORE] |
| αλήθεια (exclamative) | alíthia | αλήθεια (truth); used as a discourse particle | Really? / Truly? / By the way | Used as a conversational interjection to express surprise ("Αλήθεια;" = "Really?") or to introduce a new topic ("Αλήθεια, ήθελα να σε ρωτήσω…" = "By the way, I wanted to ask you…"). Extremely frequent in spoken Greek. | [CORE] |
| στ' αλήθεια | st' alíthia | εις (to/in) + τη (the) + αλήθεια (truth); "in truth" | truly, in truth, honestly, really | Fixed adverbial phrase used in everyday speech to intensify or affirm a statement, or to ask whether something is genuinely the case. "Στ' αλήθεια, δεν ξέρω τι να πω" = "Honestly, I don't know what to say." | [CORE] |
| η αλήθεια είναι ότι | i alíthia íne óti | η αλήθεια (the truth) + είναι (is) + ότι (that) | the truth is that… | A fixed clausal frame used to introduce a frank or corrective statement, often conceding something the speaker might prefer not to admit. Functions to signal that what follows is the speaker's genuine assessment, often contrasting with a previous claim or expectation. Extremely common in both spoken and written Greek. | [CORE] |
| λέω την αλήθεια | léo tin alíthia | λέω (I say) + την αλήθεια (the truth) | to tell the truth | The standard colloquial expression for telling the truth. Used in everyday speech, legal contexts (witness testimony), and moral discourse. Functions as both a sincere assertion and a rhetorical marker. | [CORE] |
| για την αλήθεια | ya tin alíthia | για (for) + την αλήθεια (the truth) | for the sake of truth, to be honest, truthfully | A fixed prepositional phrase used as a discourse marker to signal that the speaker is about to say something frank or corrective. Common in everyday speech and informal writing. | [CORE] |
| αλήθεια να λέμε | alíthia na léme | αλήθεια (truth) + να (subjunctive particle) + λέμε (we say) | to tell the truth, honestly speaking, let's be honest | A fixed colloquial expression used to introduce a frank or candid statement. Functions as a hedging or framing device in everyday conversation and informal writing. | [CORE] |
| κατά την αλήθεια | katá tin alíthia | κατά (according to) + την αλήθεια (the truth) | in truth, truthfully, to tell the truth | A formal or literary adverbial phrase used to introduce a candid or corrective statement. More elevated in register than η αλήθεια είναι ότι. | [CORE] |
| αλήθεια ή ψέμα | alíthia í pséma | αλήθεια (truth) + ή (or) + ψέμα (lie) | truth or lie; true or false | Used as a binary framing in everyday speech and in game contexts. Also used rhetorically to demand a definitive answer. | [CORE] |
| αλήθεια ή τόλμη | alíthia í tólmi | αλήθεια (truth) + ή (or) + τόλμη (dare, boldness) | truth or dare | The name of the party game "truth or dare" as used in Greek. A direct calque of the English game name, but using the native αλήθεια. Used in everyday speech especially among younger speakers. | [CORE] |
| αλήθεια και ψέμα | alíthia ke pséma | αλήθεια (truth) + και (and) + ψέμα (lie) | truth and lies; truth and falsehood | A paired formula used to frame a binary opposition between truthfulness and deception. Common in everyday speech, journalism, and moral discourse. | [CORE] |
| αλήθεια και δικαιοσύνη | alíthia ke dhikiosíni | αλήθεια (truth) + και (and) + δικαιοσύνη (justice) | truth and justice | A paired formula used in legal, political, and moral discourse to invoke the twin values of truthfulness and fairness. Appears in official documents, political rhetoric, ethical discourse, and the names of political organizations. | [CORE] |
| αλήθεια και συμφιλίωση | alíthia ke simfiliosi | αλήθεια (truth) + και (and) + συμφιλίωση (reconciliation) | truth and reconciliation | Used in political and transitional justice contexts, often in reference to truth and reconciliation commissions. A calque of the international term. | [CORE] |
| αλήθεια του Θεού | alíthia tu Theú | αλήθεια (truth) + του Θεού (of God, gen.) | God's truth, the truth of God, the absolute truth | Used in religious discourse and as an emphatic oath in everyday speech. "Αλήθεια του Θεού!" is used to swear that something is absolutely true. | [CORE] |
| αλήθεια ενώπιον Θεού | alíthia enópion Theú | αλήθεια (truth) + ενώπιον (before, in the presence of) + Θεού (God, genitive) | truth before God | A religious and legal formula used in oath-taking and solemn declarations to invoke divine witness to the truthfulness of a statement. Appears in ecclesiastical and formal legal contexts. | [MARGINAL] |
| αληθινός Θεός | alithinós Theós | αληθινός (true, genuine) + Θεός (God) | the true God | Used in Christian theological and liturgical discourse to distinguish the God of Christian faith from false gods or idols. Appears in the Nicene Creed and other liturgical texts. | [CORE] |
| αληθής αξία | alithís aksía | αληθής (true) + αξία (value) | true value, real value | Used in financial, economic, and philosophical contexts to refer to the actual or intrinsic value of something as opposed to its nominal or market value. | [CORE] |
| αληθής αγάπη | alithís agápi | αληθής (true) + αγάπη (love) | true love | Used in literary, religious, and everyday contexts to describe love that is genuine and deep as opposed to superficial or feigned. Common in both secular and Christian discourse. | [CORE] |

| Propositional truth and falsehood evaluation | These terms are used primarily to evaluate the truth-value of statements, propositions, testimonies, and declarations — i.e., whether what is said corresponds to what is the case. They appear characteristically in legal testimony contexts (ψευδής κατάθεση, λέω την αλήθεια), philosophical discourse about truth, and everyday contexts where someone asserts or denies that a claim is accurate. The core contrast in this group is between terms that affirm correspondence with reality and terms that deny it. | αληθής, αλήθεια, αληθεύω, αναλήθεια, αναληθής, ψευδής, ψεύδος, ψέμα, ψεύτης, ψεύτικος, ψεύδομαι, ψευδώς, λέω την αλήθεια, λέω ψέματα, ψευδής κατάθεση, ψευδής δήλωση, ψευδής ισχυρισμός, ψευδής κατηγορία, ψευδής υπόσχεση, ψευδής ταυτότητα, αλήθεια ή ψέμα, αληθής ή ψευδής, Αυτό είναι ψέμα, η αλήθεια είναι ότι, αληθής κατά τεκμήριο, εν μέρει αληθής, εν γνώσει ψευδής, αποδεδειγμένος, αδιαμφισβήτητος, διαψεύδω, διάψευση | αποδεδειγμένος, αδιαμφισβήτητος (also participate in Group 3); αλήθεια (also participates in Groups 5 and 6); ψεύτικος (also participates in Group 2) | αληθής and ψευδής are the formal/philosophical pair; αληθινός and ψέμα/ψεύτικος are the colloquial equivalents. The legal register draws heavily on ψευδής. αποδεδειγμένος and αδιαμφισβήτητος add a dimension of established or unchallengeable status. διαψεύδω belongs here because its function is to counter a false claim, not to assert truth independently. |
| Genuineness and its absence in objects and documents | These terms are applied to physical objects, artworks, documents, products, and persons to indicate whether they are what they appear or claim to be, as opposed to being copies, imitations, or counterfeits. They appear in contexts of authentication, commercial fraud, art criticism, and character evaluation. The central contrast is between terms asserting genuine origin and terms asserting fabrication or imitation. | γνήσιος, γνησιότητα, γνήσιο αντίγραφο, γνήσιο προϊόν, γνήσια υπογραφή, έλεγχος γνησιότητας, αυθεντικός, αυθεντικότητα, αυθεντικό έργο τέχνης, αυθεντική έκδοση, αυθεντικό κείμενο, αυθεντική εμπειρία, πρωτότυπο, πρωτότυπο και αντίγραφο, στο πρωτότυπο, αντίγραφο, επικυρωμένο αντίγραφο, ακριβές αντίγραφο εκ του πρωτοτύπου, πλαστός, πλαστή ταυτότητα, πλαστό διαβατήριο, πλαστή υπογραφή, πλαστά έγγραφα, πλαστογραφία, πλαστογραφώ, πλαστογράφος, πλαστό χαρτονόμισμα, πλαστό πτυχίο, πλαστά στοιχεία, νόθος, νόθο κείμενο, νόθα προϊόντα, νοθεία, νοθεύω, κίβδηλος, ψεύτικο δέρμα, ψεύτικο νόμισμα, παραποίηση, πιστοποίηση γνησιότητας, ψευδεπίγραφος, γνησιοποίηση | ψευδεπίγραφος (also participates in Group 7); ψεύτικος (also participates in Group 1); γνήσιος vs. αυθεντικός overlap considerably but are not identical | γνήσιος emphasizes legitimate origin (contrasting with νόθος) and is more common in legal and administrative contexts, while αυθεντικός emphasizes that something is the original rather than a copy or imitation and is more common in aesthetic and personal authenticity contexts. πλαστός is the standard legal term for deliberate forgery; νόθος is used more in philological and historical contexts and also covers adulteration of substances; κίβδηλος is literary and rare in everyday speech. νοθεία covers adulteration of substances as well as document falsification, giving it a broader range than πλαστογραφία. ψευδεπίγραφος belongs here in that it concerns the authenticity of attribution, but it also participates in Group 7 in that a ψευδεπίγραφος text presents itself as the work of an author it is not. |
| Verification, certification, and establishment of facts | These terms appear in contexts where a claim, document, or fact is subjected to a formal or procedural process of checking or confirmation — in scientific, legal, administrative, and journalistic registers. They describe both the act of checking (επαληθεύω, διαπιστώνω) and the formal instruments that result from such checking (πιστοποιητικό, απόδειξη, τεκμήριο). The shared feature is that truth or validity is not simply asserted but established through a recognized procedure. | επαληθεύω, επαλήθευση, επαληθεύσιμος, ανεπαλήθευτος, ανεπαλήθευτες πληροφορίες, μη επαληθεύσιμος, διαπιστώνω, διαπίστωση, πιστοποιώ, πιστοποίηση, πιστοποιητικό, πιστοποίηση ταυτότητας, τεκμήριο, τεκμηριώνω, τεκμηρίωση, τεκμηριωμένος, απόδειξη, αποδεικνύω, αποδεδειγμένος, αναπόδεικτος, έγκυρος, εγκυρότητα, έγκυρη πηγή, έγκυρο έγγραφο, έγκυρη ψήφος, άκυρος, ακυρώνω, ακύρωση, νόμιμος, παράνομος, νομιμοποίηση | αποδεδειγμένος (also participates in Group 1); έγκυρος (formal validity distinct from truth-value); τεκμήριο (indirect evidence, distinct from απόδειξη) | This group is distinguished from Group 1 by its procedural character: the terms here describe not just whether something is true but whether it has been checked, certified, or formally established. έγκυρος and άκυρος describe the status of documents and decisions with respect to formal requirements — a document can be έγκυρος without anyone having recently verified its content. τεκμήριο is specifically associated with indirect evidence from which a conclusion is inferred, distinguishing it from απόδειξη. τεκμηριωμένος is more associated with documentation and evidence-gathering; αποδεδειγμένος with demonstration and proof. |
| Credibility and trustworthiness of persons and sources | These terms are used to evaluate whether a person, institution, or source of information can be relied upon — i.e., whether their testimony, reports, or behavior merit confidence. They appear in contexts of journalistic source evaluation, legal witness assessment, and everyday character judgment. The central question is not whether a specific statement is true but whether the person or source is the kind of entity whose statements can generally be trusted. The central contrast is between αξιόπιστος and αναξιόπιστος. | αξιόπιστος, αξιοπιστία, αναξιόπιστος, αναξιοπιστία, αξιόπιστη πηγή, αξιόπιστος μάρτυρας, αξιόπιστη μαρτυρία, αξιόπιστος συνομιλητής, Δεν είναι αξιόπιστος, εμπιστοσύνη, εμπιστεύομαι, εμπιστευτικός, δυσπιστία, δύσπιστος, πιστός, πιστή μετάφραση, καλή πίστη, κακή πίστη, απιστία, άπιστος, ψήφος εμπιστοσύνης, ψήφος δυσπιστίας | πιστός (at boundary between this group and Group 2, covering both personal loyalty and fidelity of representation); καλή πίστη / κακή πίστη (legal and moral terms for intent rather than reliability of a person per se) | The terms here are relational — they describe a relationship between a person and those who evaluate them — whereas Group 1 terms are applied to propositions. εμπιστοσύνη and its family extend into interpersonal, financial, and political domains beyond epistemic evaluation. πιστός covers both personal loyalty (πιστός φίλος) and fidelity of representation (πιστή μετάφραση), which places it at the boundary between this group and Group 2. καλή πίστη / κακή πίστη are legal and moral terms for the intent behind an action rather than the reliability of a person per se, but they participate in the same evaluative register. |
| Sincerity-marking and truth-framing in discourse | These expressions function as discourse devices — they signal that what follows is a frank, sincere, or candid statement, often one that the speaker might otherwise hesitate to make. They appear at the beginning of turns or clauses, and their primary function is pragmatic rather than propositional: they frame the speaker's stance rather than evaluate the truth-value of a specific claim. Many are fixed phrases or formulaic frames. | Αλήθεια; (surprise/confirmation marker), Αλήθεια, ήθελα να σε ρωτήσω… (topic-shift marker), στ' αλήθεια, Η αλήθεια είναι ότι…, Για να λέμε την αλήθεια…, αλήθεια να λέμε, Αν θέλεις την αλήθεια…, για την αλήθεια, Πες μου την αλήθεια, αληθινά, αληθώς, Αληθώς ανέστη, κατά βάθος η αλήθεια είναι ότι…, Αυτή είναι η αλήθεια, αλήθεια του Θεού, με την αλήθεια στο στόμα, για να είμαι ακριβής, αν κατάλαβα σωστά, ακριβώς!, σωστά!, χωρίς αμφιβολία, πέρα από κάθε αμφιβολία, ουσιαστικά, φαινομενικά | αλήθεια (also participates in Groups 1 and 6); αληθινά (also participates in Group 1); ακριβώς, σωστά (also participate in their primary predicative/attributive uses in other groups) | This group is distinguished from Group 1 by function: the expressions here do not primarily evaluate a proposition as true or false but signal the speaker's commitment to candor or manage the speaker's relationship to their own utterances. The bleaching of propositional content is most complete in the topic-shift use ("Αλήθεια, ήθελα να σε ρωτήσω…") and the surprise-marker use ("Αλήθεια;"). Several items from other groups appear here in specialized discourse-management uses that are distinct from their primary predicative or attributive uses. |

#### F3_semantic_groups_table
| Group Label | Definition | Representative Expressions | Overlapping / Ambiguous Items | Boundary Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Factual truth assertion and denial | These expressions are used in everyday and formal discourse to affirm or deny that something is true or real as a matter of fact — that it actually happened, actually exists, or actually is the case. They appear in contexts of confirming reports, correcting misconceptions, and responding to doubt. The core items in this group participate in interrogative truth-checks (*totoo ba?*), discourse-initial framing (*ang totoo*, *sa katotohanan*), and particle-marked epistemic stance constructions (*totoo nga pala*, *totoo naman*). They are applied to propositions, events, and states of affairs. | *totoo*; *katotohanan*; *totoong-totoo*; *hindi totoo*; *totoo ba?*; *totoo naman*; *totoo nga*; *totoo pala*; *totoo nga pala*; *totoo pa rin*; *hindi naman totoo*; *totoo man o hindi*; *totoo na*; *totoo o hindi*; *ang totoo*; *ang totoo nito*; *sa katotohanan*; *ang katotohanan ay*; *walang katotohanan*; *may katotohanan*; *totoo ang lahat*; *totoo sa buhay*; *totoong kwento*; *totoong pangyayari*; *naniniwala akong totoo ito*; *kung totoo man o hindi*; *aktuwal*; *aktuwal na nangyari*; *makatotohanan*; *hindi makatotohanan*; *makatotohanang-makatotohanan* [MARGINAL]; *makatotohanang pelikula* | *sa katotohanan* also appears in Group 2; *katotohanan* also appears in Group 2 and Group 10; *makatotohanan* and *totoo sa buhay* also appear in Group 10 | *Totoo* is the dominant item and the only one participating in the full range of particle-marked epistemic stance constructions. *Aktuwal* is more restricted in register than *totoo*. *Sa katotohanan* and *ang totoo* function as discourse-framing devices rather than simple predicates. *Makatotohanan* and *totoo sa buhay* are primarily aesthetic/representational evaluation rather than propositional truth-assertion. *Totoo naman* and *totoo na* are pragmatically specialized and could be considered a sub-pattern within this group rather than fully independent items. |
